newsitem.title: USA: UPS says union seeks to avoid pension issue.
newsitem.headline: UPS says union seeks to avoid pension issue.

text.p: UPS said Monday that that comments from its striking Teamsters about part-time job opportunities and subcontracting are a "smokescreen" to avoid discussion on the larger issue of employee pensions.
In a statement released Monday afternoon, the company made the following comments regarding the issue of part-time and full-time jobs:
-- The average part-time worker at UPS earns $11 an hour, with about 60,000 part-time workers earning more than $16,000 annually.
-- All part-time employees at UPS enjoy comprehensive benefits packages.
-- Over the past four years, more than 13,000 UPS part-time workers moved into full-time positions.
-- No full-time employee at UPS has ever been replaced by a part-time employee.
-- UPS has offered to create an additional 11,000 opportunities for part-time employees to move into full-time jobs over the next five years.
UPS also has proposed language in its final contract offer that guarantees no UPS driver would ever be replaced by a subcontractor.
UPS also said its contract proposal offers to increase the monthly pension benefit for full- and part-time UPS employees by an average of 50 percent.

The changes, said the company, would provide that UPS retirees be covered under new pension plans created outside the existing Teamsters multi-employer pension system. The penison system is one of issues over which contract talks collapsed.
